no model call composes it\u0022,\u0022The reply\\u0027s text is shown as quoted data on the row and in h9k task show, never placed into any prompt by this path\u0022,\u0022A mention from anyone other than the pull request\\u0027s author, and a pull request author\\u0027s mention on a task with an unwalked report, behave exactly as they do today\u0022,\u0022Unit tests over the decision, with no database, no branch, and no GitHub, cover the author-reply case (row, no run) and both unchanged cases; Decide from that whether a claim and a task run are needed at all. A full run that analyzes the whole pull request just to read one comment is the wrong default. Motivating case: arx-platform#2166 / bc7d2572 on 2026-10-01, where Brian\\u0027s reply tagging @taylor-dennison woke his own review task and ran a follow-up that found nothing.\\n\\nBrian, 2026-10-02 (f894d344 discovery question 1): the three follow-up laps on 2026-09-29 (AgelessRx/arx-platform #2170, #2172, #2174, Taylor answering Brian\\u0027s reviews, $5.28 recorded) were not useful as runs; what was useful was knowing what Taylor had replied. So this card keeps a view of the reply and drops the run. Brian chose option A: the reply\\u0027s own opening lines, no model call. Option B, a short summary written by a tool-less model call, is a possible follow-on only if Brian asks for it; do not build it here. Where it lives: AutoPrReviewEngine.AttachMentionAsync and its dispatch gates (around 2241-2380 at e03c7d7e6); PullRequestMentionSearch.Author already carries the author\\u0027s login and account id.
